summary:
Reviewed and fixed. The builder's JKMODE.EXE (md5 19a53200a436ac427f7351b1af654608) would have written the wrong displayMode on every box where it does not refuse, so that build must not be staged. It left out two things the games do; I found both by re-reading JK.EXE and JKM.EXE and confirmed them by running the games' own code under emulation.

1. Both games SORT the mode list before storing it. After the two enumeration passes and the 64-entry cap, the device-open routine calls the MSVC runtime qsort: JK 0x422797 calls qsort 0x513060 with comparator 0x4249d0; MotS 0x4258da uses 0x56c510 and 0x427b00, identical code. The sort order is bpp, then width, then height, and displayMode indexes the SORTED copy. The builder's DF2 indices (45, 34 and 58 on .123, .145 and .195) are enumeration positions. In the game's real list those entries are 1680x1050x32, 640x480x32 and 1776x1000x32, so the helper would have started DF2 in 3D at 32 bpp, a state the game's own menu never offers. The correct DF2 indices are 31, 33 and 39.

2. MotS drops high-resolution 8-bpp modes. Its pass-2 callback (0x428f9e) returns without storing or counting any mode whose width is 1400 or more and whose lPitch equals its width. DF2's callback has no such test. I checked XP SP3's own ddraw.dll (from the fleet image): it reports lPitch = width*bpp/8 and keeps enumerating after that non-zero return. So on XP every 8-bpp mode 1400 or wider is dropped. The builder's MotS index for .123 (43) is past the end of the game's 42-entry list, which the game reads without a range check. On .145 its index would have selected a 32-bpp mode.

Fixes, all in provisioning/patches/jk-helper/:
- jklogic.h now applies the MotS filter to the real lPitch and sorts with an exact port of the game's qsort and comparator. The exact port matters because the comparator is not a consistent ordering when ModeX and ordinary 320-wide modes are both present, as on .240, so only the same algorithm gives the game's order.
- jkmode.c passes lPitch and a per-game filter flag, and sorts right after the passes, as the game does before copying the list. It refuses with exit 7 if a mode's bpp cannot be read.
- jkmode.c also gained a per-box off switch, HKLM\Software\RetroAgent JkMode (REG_DWORD) = 0. It is read-only and checked before anything else. It exists because the helper re-applies the mode before every launch.
- New file emu_modelist.py runs the games' own callbacks, qsort and comparator from the staged binaries under unicorn.

The C port matches the game's code entry for entry on all 16 box/game/pitch cases and on 400 random lists. Correct indices:
- DF2: 31 / 33 / 39 on .123 / .145 / .195.
- MotS: 26 / 27 on .123 / .145, and 33 on .195 (36 if Win7 pads the pitch).
- .240 is refused for both games: 1920x1080x16 is enumerated at position 76 (DF2) and 73 (MotS), past the 64 modes the game keeps.

The builder's other claims hold against the disassembly: the coop flags per pass, the 64/16/4 caps, the device and 3D records and the selection loops, REG_BINARY types, the key wipe when Version is not "0.1", the zero GUID for the primary device, no range check, and the 3D-tick pair.

New build: JKMODE.EXE, md5 ee50a1b453e1f72dd27dbd1a9c712e9b, 13,824 bytes. It builds deterministically, imports only KERNEL32/USER32/ADVAPI32, has subsystem version 4.0 and no SSE or cmov. apply.py --check passes with 31 JK and 30 MotS asserted rows, including the new sort, comparator, qsort and filter rows. apply.py --build passes. No game file is patched and nothing was written to the share or a box. JKMODE has still never run on Windows.
launcher_changes_needed: scripts/fleet/stage-fleetres.py TITLES: add two entries, with the JKMODE game token in the recipe's `mod` slot: "JediKnightDF2": {"new": {"Play Jedi Knight.bat": ("JK.EXE", "df2")}, "launch_txt_line0": ("Play Jedi Knight.bat", "Jedi Knight - Dark Forces II", "JK.EXE")} and "JediKnightMotS": {"new": {"Play Mysteries of the Sith.bat": ("JKM.EXE", "mots")}, "launch_txt_line0": ("Play Mysteries of the Sith.bat", "Jedi Knight - Mysteries of the Sith", "JKM.EXE")}. payload() already stages FLEETRES.EXE and FLEETRES.BAT for every TITLES entry, so nothing else is needed there.

scripts/fleet/stage-fleetres.py new_launcher(): add `elif title in ("JediKnightDF2", "JediKnightMotS"): text = NEW_JEDI.format(...)` BEFORE the id Tech 3 fall-through. Without it both titles silently get a Quake III launcher. NEW_JEDI must render, after crlf(), exactly what provisioning/patches/jk-helper/apply.py launcher_text(title) returns. The reference files are ~/.retro-fleet/patch-out/jk-helper/<Title>/<launcher>, md5 26ff7857f052f09715c12708b08e06e7 (DF2) and b73912116edfa4f28816aa34af4ebfe3 (MotS). The functional lines, in order: `cd /d "%~dp0"` / `call "%~dp0FLEETRES.BAT"` / `if exist "%~dp0JKMODE.EXE" "%~dp0JKMODE.EXE" df2 %FR_W% %FR_H% > "%~dp0JKMODE.LOG" 2>&1` (`mots` for MotS) / `start "" JK.EXE` (JKM.EXE) / `exit`. Use single % throughout. There are no parentheses anywhere and no set values or blocks.

tests/python/test_fleetres_staging.py: add sf.NEW_JEDI to the template lists that the FR_* fallback check (the `used.update(... sf.NEW_IDTECH3)` lines around 270-272) and _all_generated_lines() (around line 391) scan, so the no-doubled-percent and FLEETRES-fallback checks cover the new template.

Share ordering. Publish JKMODE.EXE into both trees FIRST with `python3 provisioning/patches/jk-helper/apply.py --publish`. That script should be the single owner of JKMODE.EXE: it refuses unless the staged JK.EXE/JKM.EXE md5 is the one the helper was written for, writes one file at a time through sharewrite.py, backs up a differing copy first, and skips a current one. THEN run stage-fleetres.py; it writes FLEETRES, the launcher and, last, launch.txt. launch.txt must never name a launcher that is not in the tree yet, or the validator fails.

JediKnightDF2/launch.txt line 0 becomes `Play Jedi Knight.bat<TAB>Jedi Knight - Dark Forces II<TAB>JK.EXE`, and JediKnightMotS becomes `Play Mysteries of the Sith.bat<TAB>Jedi Knight - Mysteries of the Sith<TAB>JKM.EXE`. The display names and icons are unchanged, so each .lnk keeps its name and icon. Both lines are far under the 1023-byte read.

Keep FR_W/FR_H, not FR_W43. The user asked for 1920x1080. If the hardware check shows the 4:3 Sith renderer unacceptably stretched, switch the JKMODE arguments to %FR_W43% %FR_H43%. JKMODE refuses cleanly (exit 3) if that mode is not in the game's list.

GAMERES (agent/shared/gameres.h): add NO rule. The value is a per-box index into a sorted list that only a DirectDraw enumeration on the box can produce. install.reg does not carry these values, and FLEETRES only sets environment variables for these titles, so there is no shared file for FLEETRES and GAMERES to fight over. The game's own clean Quit rewrites the same values, which is harmless.

Per-box escape hatch, no code change needed. If a box lists 1920x1080x16 but the game's 3D fails there, `REGWRITE HKLM Software\RetroAgent JkMode REG_DWORD 0` and read it back. JKMODE then logs `RESULT DISABLED` and touches nothing. Also clear the values it wrote earlier (`EXEC reg delete "HKLM\Software\LucasArts Entertainment Company\JediKnight\v1.0" /v displayMode /f`, and the same for b3DAccel; the MotS key for MotS), or pick a working mode in Setup and Quit cleanly.

provisioning/fleetres/PER-TITLE-STATUS.md rows JediKnightDF2 and JediKnightMotS (currently 'incapable'), once verified on hardware: '1080p via JKMODE.EXE (per-box index into the game's sorted list) on .123/.145/.195; .240 refused - 1920x1080x16 enumerated at position 76 (DF2) / 73 (MotS), past the 64 modes the game keeps'.

After every lane has published: bump Files/Games-Library/_deploy_generation.txt ONCE (scripts/fleet/autodeploy.py), or no provisioned box re-syncs these titles. Then run scripts/validate-staged-library.py and stage-fleetres.py --check.
tests:
`python3 -m pytest tests/python/test_patch_jk-helper.py` (tests/pytest.ini adds -q):
- System python3: 50 passed, 8 skipped. The 8 skips are loud: unicorn/pefile are missing, so the game-code cross-checks cannot run.
- Scratch venv with unicorn and pefile: 58 passed. There, the 8 cross-checks run the games' own callbacks, qsort and comparator from JK.EXE/JKM.EXE on the share and compare every stored entry with jklogic.h.
- Evidence: .claude/evidence-1080p/build-jk-helper/pytest.txt.

Added or changed:
- Per-box indices pinned to the game-code values: DF2 31/33/39/cut; MotS 26/27/33/cut, and 27/28/36/cut with a 32-byte-aligned pitch.
- A regression guard that the builder's first indices select 1680x1050x32 (DF2 on .123) or run past MotS's 42 entries.
- Comparator semantics, including the ModeX special case.
- The MotS filter: exactly 1400 is dropped, 1399 is kept, a padded pitch is kept, and DF2 is unaffected.
- The full 64-entry sorted order on .240, pinned from the game's code. This is the case where only an exact qsort port reproduces the order.
- Unknown-bpp detection.
- Source pins:
  - the sort runs after coop 8 and before QueryInterface;
  - lPitch (+0x10) and the filter flag reach the callback;
  - exit 7;
  - the new offset rows;
  - the JkMode switch is read-only and checked before ddraw is loaded or the key is opened for writing.
- Five --publish tests against a temporary fake library and a fake sharewrite.py that only logs its argv. They cover: each file is put once; a differing share copy is backed up to _patches/<Title>/originals-2026-09-29/ first and a current one is skipped; publishing stops at the first failure; a mismatched staged exe is refused before any call; --dry-run is forwarded. No share, NAS or vault was touched.
- The probe was updated for the new jk_mode_offer signature. The builder's stale tests were corrected: the cap test, the ModeX-same-width test, and the test pinning 45/43, which asserted an index equal to the enumeration position.

Also run:
- `apply.py --check` returned rc=0 (31 JK and 30 MotS rows hold, both md5s and sizes match).
- `apply.py --build` returned rc=0, plus two more builds to scratch: identical md5 ee50a1b453e1f72dd27dbd1a9c712e9b.
- A 400-trial randomized differential of the C port against the emulated game code: 0 mismatches (review/fuzz_port_vs_game_code.txt).
- An independent pefile check of every offset row.

Not run, by rule: --publish and --install-server against anything real, and JKMODE.EXE on Windows.
risks: JKMODE.EXE has still never executed on Windows. The mode-list logic is proven against the games' own code, but the COM, registry and window plumbing has not run. Run it first in the build VM (expect a clean exit-4 refusal), then as a dry run on each box.

The MotS index depends on the lPitch the runtime reports for 8-bpp modes. On XP it is verified: XP SP3's ddraw.dll reports width*bpp/8, so the expected indices are 26 on .123 and 27 on .145. Win7's ddraw (.195) was not examined, so the index there is 33 or 36. JKMODE reads the real value, so it is correct either way; only the expected figure in the plan varies.

16-bit Direct3D at 1920x1080 has never been run on these cards, and the Sith renderer is 4:3, so the picture may be stretched. Because JKMODE re-applies the mode before every launch, a box where this fails stays broken until someone sets HKLM\Software\RetroAgent JkMode=0 AND clears the stored displayMode/b3DAccel, or picks a working mode in-game and quits cleanly.

.240 is refused permanently: 1920x1080x16 is enumerated at position 76 (DF2) and 73 (MotS), past the 64 modes the game keeps. Reaching 1080p there needs a smaller driver mode list or a JK.EXE/JKM.EXE callback patch; neither was built.

The builder's original build (md5 19a53200a436ac427f7351b1af654608) is wrong on every box where it does not refuse: DF2 would start in 3D at 32 bpp, and MotS would get indices past the end of its list or a 32-bpp mode. Stage only ee50a1b453e1f72dd27dbd1a9c712e9b; apply.py --publish reads the current manifest.

Multi-adapter boxes: JKMODE, like the game's own 3D checkbox, prefers an add-on 3D DirectDraw device. On .143 (GeForce 6800 + V5 5500), or on a box with a Voodoo 2, that may route the game to the 3dfx card. Do a dry run there before pushing.

Win9x: the launcher is cmd.exe dialect (%~dp0, cd /d, start "") and it replaces a shortcut that points straight at the exe. Both titles are gated or absent on .243 today, but if the gate ever admits them there, the .bat would fail where JK.EXE works.

Every launch takes an exclusive DirectDraw cooperative level on a hidden 1x1 window for a moment. ddenum did the same on all four LCD boxes without side effects; on Win7 it may flicker or pause DWM briefly.

Entries with equal sort keys (for example two 16-bpp pixel formats at 1920x1080) resolve to whichever the ported qsort puts first. That is the same entry the game's qsort puts first, and both are 1920x1080 16 bpp.
A refusal is visible only in JKMODE.LOG beside the exe (RESULT REFUSED/FAILED/DISABLED). The launcher still starts the game, which keeps its stored values.
hw_verification_plan:
Prerequisites:
- JKMODE.EXE ee50a1b453e1f72dd27dbd1a9c712e9b is published by apply.py --publish.
- stage-fleetres.py has written FLEETRES.EXE/BAT, both Play .bats and launch.txt.
- Each LCD box has been purged (`rd /s /q C:\Games\JediKnightDF2`, the same for MotS, plus their .lnk) and re-synced with GAMESYNC RESET + START. Quote failed_files == 0, and titles_total == the library count for that box.
- Before anything, REGREAD both keys (HKLM\Software\LucasArts Entertainment Company\JediKnight\v1.0 and ...LLC\Mysteries of the Sith\v1.0) and save them. Also read HKLM\Software\RetroAgent JkMode; it should be absent.

0. Build VM first; no fleet box is at risk.
- Upload JKMODE.EXE to the XP build VM (agent on 127.0.0.1:19898) and `EXEC <path>\JKMODE.EXE df2 1024 768 dry list`.
- Expected: the device list and the sorted mode list print, and the result is `REFUSED ... no Direct3D device passes` with exit 4 (the VM's Cirrus has no D3D HAL).
- This proves the COM and registry plumbing runs without a crash.

1. Dry runs on each LCD box: `EXEC "C:\Games\JediKnightDF2\JKMODE.EXE" df2 1920 1080 dry list`, then `... mots ...` in the MotS directory.
- DF2 expected, from the game's own code on the measured lists:
  - .123: `displayMode = 31`, keeps 47 of 47.
  - .145: 33, keeps 50 of 50.
  - .195: 39, keeps 60 of 60.
  - .240: `REFUSED: 1920x1080x16 is enumerated at position 76 of 78`, exit 3.
- MotS expected:
  - .123: 26 (42 of 42).
  - .145: 27 (44 of 44).
  - .195: 33 (54 of 54), or 36 (57 of 57) if Win7 pads the pitch.
  - .240: REFUSED at position 73 of 75.
- The 3D line must say `usable`, and REGREAD must be unchanged.
- Any other number means the box's list differs from the measured fixture: compare the `list` output with fixtures/ddenum_<box>_df2_sequence.txt before going further.

2. Real launch through the shortcut path: `EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\JediKnightDF2" "Play Jedi Knight.bat"`.
- `DOWNLOAD C:\Games\JediKnightDF2\JKMODE.LOG`. It must end `RESULT OK 1920x1080 16bpp 3D, displayMode=<index from step 1>, 4 value(s) changed`, and `0 value(s) changed` on a second launch.
- REGREAD must show displayMode = that index (REG_BINARY), b3DAccel = 01000000, and 16-byte displayDeviceGUID (all zeros for the primary) and 3DDeviceGUID.

3. The decisive check, which the old dry-run figures could not provide: the GAME must read that index as 1920x1080 16bpp.
- MotS on XP (16-bit GUI, screenshot-able): Esc, Players Ok (558 449), Setup (544 409), Display (318 99).
- 'Enable 3D Acceleration' must already be ticked, and the SELECTED 'Available Video Modes' row must read '1920x1080 16bpp' (scroll with the down arrow at 160 381).
- DF2: the same check; its 8-bit GUI photographs with confetti colours, so judge the geometry.
- Leave with Cancel (99 449).
- If the highlighted row is anything else, stop and set JkMode=0 on that box.

4. Enter a level. A fullscreen SCREENSHOT 0 on XP must show a 1920x1080 3D frame; record whether it is stretched. If the stretch is unacceptable, switch the launcher to %FR_W43% %FR_H43%.
- .195 (Win7) cannot be photographed fullscreen: use JKMODE.LOG, REGREAD, and DISPLAYCFG get while the game runs (expect 1920x1080).

5. .240: JKMODE.LOG must say REFUSED; the game starts on its stored or default mode; nothing in the registry changes.

6. If 3D at 1080p fails on any box:
- `REGWRITE HKLM Software\RetroAgent JkMode REG_DWORD 0`, then read it back.
- Delete displayMode and b3DAccel with `EXEC reg delete "<key>" /v <name> /f` and read them back absent.
- Relaunch: JKMODE.LOG must say `RESULT DISABLED` and the game must start as before.

7. .143, only if the titles deploy there: dry run first. If it picks the V5 5500 as the add-on 3D device, stop and decide before a real launch.

8. Leave each box clean:
- Quit the game properly (Quit writes the same values), or `taskkill /f /im "JK.EXE"` / `"JKM.EXE"`.
- After a taskkill, restore the desktop with ChangeDisplaySettings(NULL,0) (regmode.c) and confirm DISPLAYCFG get = 1920x1080.

What must NOT change:
- The DirectPlay LAN join: host on .123, join from .240 via 'Internet TCP/IP Connection For DirectPlay' with a blank Locate Session, screenshots of both, as in the 2026-08-31 proof.
- CD Path, InstallType, InstallData and Version in HKLM.
- The persisted desktop mode.
- The .lnk names and icons (launch.txt display names and JK.EXE/JKM.EXE icons are unchanged), and the staged player\fleet profile.
review_notes:
WHAT I VERIFIED, independently of the builder's own mapper:
- Re-hashed both staged originals: md5 and size match.
- Re-checked every offset row with pefile (26 JK + 25 MotS originally, 31 + 30 now): VA-to-file-offset and bytes all hold.
- Disassembled both binaries (capstone/objdump) and checked the semantics behind each row, not only the bytes:
  - the DirectDrawEnumerate callback: 16-entry cap, zero GUID for the primary, coop 0x11, DDCAPS_3D, coop 8;
  - both mode callbacks and the 64 cap;
  - the device-list builder, with the 'Window Display Device' at entry 0;
  - the per-device loop: a Direct3D failure fails the whole list;
  - the EnumDevices record: diffed byte-identical between the games modulo addresses, with every field matched to jk_d3d_from_desc;
  - the load routine: GUID resolution, both selection loops, b3DAccel forced to 0 without a usable device, displayMode used unchecked;
  - the 3D-tick handler;
  - the REG_BINARY writers and any-type readers;
  - the Version strcmp against "0.1" with RegDeleteKeyA on mismatch.
- The load routines of the two games are identical except for one extra MotS registry read.
- --publish matches sharewrite.py's `put <local> <dest> [--dry-run]` interface, backs up before replacing, and stops at the first failure. I proved this with fake-share tests, never by running it.
- Nothing was written to the share: no JKMODE, launcher or FLEETRES file (case-insensitive), no _patches/Jedi* directory, launch.txt unchanged, exes unchanged. No box was touched.
- No game data or patched binary is under the worktree. The files are our own C and Python, the ddenum measurements, and short byte signatures for --check. __pycache__ is git-ignored. Nothing was committed.
- The launchers have no parentheses and are CRLF. There is no FLEETRES-vs-GAMERES shared file. The Sith engine is peer-hosted DirectPlay with no dedicated server, so --install-server correctly reports not applicable.

WHAT WAS WRONG, AND WHAT I CHANGED (only in provisioning/patches/jk-helper/ and tests/python/test_patch_jk-helper.py):
1. CRITICAL: the game SORTS its capped mode list. JK 0x422797 calls qsort 0x513060 with comparator 0x4249d0; MotS 0x4258da uses 0x56c510/0x427b00, identical code. It sorts by bpp, then width, then height, with a ModeX special case, and displayMode indexes the sorted copy. The diagnosis (ddenum) and the builder both used enumeration order.
   Fix: jklogic.h gained jk_mode_cmp and jk_sort_modes, an exact port of the MSVC 4-6 qsort.c. I confirmed it is that routine from the disassembly: CUTOFF 8 shortsort, middle pivot, lo/hi stacks. jkmode.c sorts right after the passes.
2. CRITICAL: MotS's pass-2 callback (0x428f9e) drops modes with width >= 1400 and lPitch == width without counting them. DF2's has no such test (0x425e6e).
   Fix: jk_mode_offer takes pitch and a hires8_filter flag (df2 0, mots 1), and mode_cb passes DDSURFACEDESC +0x10.
   I confirmed from XP SP3's own ddraw.dll (Files/OS/XPSP3-FLEET/I386/DDRAW.DL_) that XP reports lPitch = w*bpp>>3 and continues the enumeration on any non-zero return.
3. PROOF: emu_modelist.py (new) runs the real callbacks, qsort and comparator from the share under unicorn. The C port equals it entry for entry on all 16 box/game/pitch cases and on 400 random lists. A test cross-checks it live when unicorn is present and skips loudly otherwise.
   Correct 1920x1080x16 indices: DF2 31/33/39 (the builder had 45/34/58, which are 1680x1050x32 / 640x480x32 / 1776x1000x32); MotS 26/27/33 (the builder had 43 on .123, past the 42-entry end).
4. Added refusal exit 7: the chosen device holds a mode with neither PAL8 nor RGB, whose sort key the game takes from stale memory, so no index is knowable.
5. Added the per-box off switch HKLM\Software\RetroAgent JkMode=0. It is read-only and checked before ddraw or any write, because the helper re-applies before every launch. JKMODE_VERSION is now 1.1.
6. apply.py:
   - 5 new check rows per game: the sort call, the comparator, the qsort cutoff and pivot, the MotS filter, and DF2's lack of one.
   - MEASURED_DF2_1080P (which held enumeration positions and was mislabelled as measured) is replaced by GAME_CODE_1080P, with its provenance.
   - The docstring and launcher comment text are corrected; the functional launcher lines are unchanged.
7. Tests: stale expectations corrected, and new logic, source, publish and emulation tests added (58 in total).
8. Evidence:
   - The builder's stale evidence moved to build-jk-helper/review/builder-original/.
   - Fresh check, build, pytest, ABI, manifest and launcher files at the top level.
   - Proofs in review/: sort_and_filter.asm.txt, game_code_sorted_lists.txt, xp_ddraw_enumdisplaymodes.asm.txt, and fuzz_port_vs_game_code.{py,txt}.

LAUNCHER HAND-OFF CORRECTIONS:
- The recipe shape is spelled out: tuples with the game token in `mod`, plus launch_txt_line0.
- new_launcher() needs its branch before the id Tech 3 fall-through, or both titles silently get a Quake III launcher.
- test_fleetres_staging.py must list NEW_JEDI.
- payload() is automatic.
- JKMODE.EXE has one owner (apply.py --publish), which must run before launch.txt changes.
